title: How to Find Strong Construction Stocks Slated for Positive Earnings Surprises
author: Zacks.Com
description: The article explains how to identify construction stocks poised for earnings surprises using the Zacks Earnings ESP tool, which compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Two construction stocks highlighted are Quanta Services (PWR) with a +2.66% ESP and Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), and Sterling Infrastructure (STRL) with a +0.80% ESP and Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), both expected to report earnings in late October 2026.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Positive Earnings ESP of +2.66% indicates the Most Accurate Estimate ($5.14) exceeds the Zacks Consensus Estimate ($5.01), suggesting potential for an earnings beat. Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) combined with positive ESP historically resulted in 70% positive surprises.

Positive Earnings ESP of +0.80% with Most Accurate Estimate ($6.12) above Zacks Consensus Estimate ($6.07). Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) is stronger than PWR's ranking, indicating outperformance potential relative to the broader market and higher probability of earnings beat.

title: Can Quanta Overcome Macro Headwinds With Record Project Demand?
author: Na
description: Quanta Services (PWR) reported strong Q2 2026 revenues of $9.6 billion with a record $53 billion backlog, driven by infrastructure demand and power grid modernization. However, the company faces headwinds from inflation, labor shortages, and permitting delays that could pressure margins. Recent acquisitions are expected to add $1.2-$1.4 billion in 2026 revenues. Success will depend on effective backlog conversion and project execution amid macroeconomic uncertainties.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q2 revenues of $9.6 billion, record $53 billion backlog, double-digit EBITDA and EPS growth, and strategic acquisitions expected to contribute $1.2-$1.4 billion in 2026 revenues demonstrate solid growth momentum and market positioning in infrastructure modernization.

Benefits from growing public infrastructure, transportation, water and environmental projects supported by long-term government funding through its asset-light engineering, design, consulting and program management expertise.

Well-positioned to benefit from broadband expansion, fiber deployments and network upgrades by major telecom operators, sustaining demand for specialty contracting services in the communications infrastructure cycle.

title: Is iShares U.S. Infrastructure ETF (IFRA) a Strong ETF Right Now?
author: Na
description: IFRA is a smart beta ETF launched in 2018 that tracks the NYSE FactSet U.S. Infrastructure Index with over $4 billion in assets. Managed by BlackRock, it offers low expenses at 0.30% and focuses on U.S. companies with infrastructure exposure. The fund has performed well year-to-date with a 9.59% gain and maintains a 1.79% dividend yield, with top holdings including Caterpillar, Quanta Services, and Union Pacific.

title: Why Quanta Services (PWR) Dipped More Than Broader Market Today
author: Na
description: Quanta Services (PWR) declined 1.53% in the latest session, underperforming the S&P 500. The company is expected to report earnings on October 29, 2026, with anticipated EPS of $5.01 (up 50.45% YoY) and revenue of $10.99 billion (up 43.95% YoY). However, PWR trades at a premium valuation with a Forward P/E of 38.47 versus the industry average of 22.28, and holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the company shows strong earnings growth expectations (50.45% EPS growth, 43.95% revenue growth), it carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and trades at a significant valuation premium (Forward P/E of 38.47 vs. industry average of 22.28). The PEG ratio of 1.75 also exceeds the industry average of 1.1, suggesting the stock may be overvalued relative to growth prospects. Recent stock performance has been mixed with a 1.53% daily decline.

title: Can EMCOR's Turnaround and Petrochemical Work Lift Industrial Growth?
author: Na
description: EMCOR Group Inc. (EME) reported strong second quarter 2026 results for its U.S. Industrial Services segment, with revenues climbing 25.9% to $353.8 million and returning to profitability with $9.6 million in operating income. Growth was driven by higher turnaround activity, increased petrochemical project volume, and progress on a large solar project. The company trades at a premium valuation with a forward P/E of 20.16 and carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 25.9% revenue growth, return to profitability after prior-year loss, improved operating margins (2.7% vs -0.1%), and Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating. Stock has outperformed industry and S&P 500 YTD with 19.7% gains.
Mentioned as a key competitor with strong capabilities and customer relationships, but exposure to utility capital spending timing creates growth variability.

Noted as a competitor with diversified infrastructure platform benefiting from multiple investment themes, but project timing variability across end markets creates near-term deferrals in some segments.
